newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine troops intensify fight vs Moslem rebels.
newsitem.headline: Philippine troops intensify fight vs Moslem rebels.

text.p: The Philippines army on Thursday rescued dozens of hostages in a bloody battle in the troubled southern island of Mindanao as fighting intensified against Moslem separatists.
Defence Secretary Renato de Villa told reporters that four rebels and two soldiers had died in the fighting on Thursday morning over the hostages. A number of others were wounded.

He gave no other details, but a local police chief said at least 60 people travelling early in the morning by bus on a country road near the city of Cotabato had been grabbed by some 200 armed members of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF).

About 20,000 villagers have fled their homes and least 45 people, mostly rebels, have been killed in more than a week of fighting that erupted after MILF rebels briefly took over a state-owned oil and gas exploration site on the island.

Deputy commander of the southern military command, Brigadier-General Ronnie Benedicto, said the military had already sent in six MG-520 rocket-firing helicopters to support its offensive in the area in central Mindanao.
It has also closed a vital road link between the cities of Cotabato and Davao.
MILF leaders have warned that the military's latest offensive could scupper peace talks that were due to restart this weekend.
The MILF, estimated to have 8,000 armed fighters, is battling for independence for Mindanao, an ancestral Moslem homeland in the predominantly Christian Philippines.
It stayed out of a peace treaty signed late last year by Manila and the mainstream Islamic separatist group, the Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF).
Local officials urged Manila to try to end the fighting.

"We are appealing to his excellency (President Fidel Ramos) to initiate some measures wherein military operations can be stopped," Tommy Ala, chief of staff for the acting governor of the Autonomous Region for Moslem Mindanao, told Reuters.
Defence Secretary de Villa said Manila, whose peace talks with the MILF have so far failed to bear any fruit, realised fighting alone would not bring a solution.
"This problem will not be solved with the use of heavy armaments," he said.
